items.name: b11642
items.body:
<details open>

server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache (#30498)

* server: save only restorable slot states to the prompt cache

The idle-slot save loop stores every idle slot whenever a task starts,
while only completion tasks restore from the prompt cache. Rerank,
embedding, decision and infill states fill the cache up to its limit
without ever being read back, and slots already cached are offered
again at every task start.

Each slot now tracks with cache_pending whether its state is restorable
and missing from the cache: a completion release or an explicit slot
restore sets it, prompt_save consumes it, prompt_clear resets it. Both
save paths share this rule, and the LRU path restores only for
completion tasks.

* server: test that decision slots skip the prompt cache

Decision tasks never mark their slot as cacheable, so starting new
tasks must not save their idle slots to the RAM prompt cache, with or
without a unified KV cache.

* server: restore any reusing task from the prompt cache

Embedding and rerank tasks never reuse their state, so their slots are
cleared on release like child slots and the cache only holds states
that a later task can restore. Infill and decision tasks now restore
from the cache too, which replaces the cache_pending flag.

Decision models disable the prompt cache unless --cache-ram is given,
since their states seldom repeat.

</details>

<details open>

opencl: support CLAMP on non-contiguous views (#30186)

The clamp kernel indexed source and destination as one flat contiguous array, so
a strided view as input (the new CLAMP v=1 case) read the wrong elements. Add a
strided kernel_clamp_nc, as the other unary ops have, and take it whenever the
source is not contiguous.

</details>

items.name: b11636
items.body:
<details open>

sycl: IQ3 code reorder (#29107)

* sycl: persistent IQ3_S/IQ3_XXS weight reorder for SYCL decode and prefill

Add persistent reordered weight layouts for IQ3_S and IQ3_XXS. Weights
are reordered once at load time; the reordered MMVQ dot products then
walk dense super-blocks with dp4a and SWAR sign expansion instead of
gathering bits from the interleaved standard layout. Reorder-aware
dequantization feeds the batched prefill GEMMs so prompt processing
sees the same benefit.

Also harden the oneDNN build check: a missing DNNL package or a
CPU-only DNNL build now fails at configure time instead of silently
producing a degraded backend.

Measured on Intel Arc Pro B70 with Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S (MTP),
-ngl 999 -b 4096 -ub 1024 -fa on:

tg256 @ 0 ctx      12.92 -> 23.54 tok/s (+82%)
tg256 @ 9,216      12.33 -> 21.69 tok/s (+76%)
tg256 @ 64,000      9.76 -> 14.91 tok/s (+53%)
pp8192             833.9  -> 833.6 tok/s (flat)

Qwen3.5-9B Q4_K_M / Q3_K_M are unchanged within noise (largest delta
-0.5% pp, tg flat), so standard quants are not affected.

The MMVQ GLU fusion widening and rms_norm+scale fusion are
intentionally not part of this change; master already carries them
via #28931.

* removing wait as per review request

* sycl : fix fusion.cpp line ending

</details>
